subject: SLO discovery: latency & context window — UX impact and fallback options

Subject: SLO discovery: latency & context window — UX impact and fallback options

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the perf POC correctly.

Summary of what I heard:
- Primary UX: interactive clinician assistant inside your EHR, where clinicians type queries and get generated summaries + suggested next steps. Median session length today: ~3 turns, but some sessions include long patient notes.
- Target latency: 200 ms p95 for token streaming to the UI during interactive editing; 500 ms p95 acceptable for full-response generation in background tasks.
- Throughput: peak concurrency ~75 active users during morning rounds; typical sustained QPS for generation ~18–25 qps, burst to ~120 qps for backfill operations.
- Context window needs: input (notes + chart) up to ~6k tokens; target output up to 1.5k tokens typical, occasional 3k.

Key clarifying questions for the POC (would appreciate short answers or a sample dataset):
1) When you say 6k tokens of context, how often do you hit the 6k bound today vs 3–4k? (a percentage or rough frequency helps).
2) Are streaming responses surfaced token-by-token to the clinician UI, or do you buffer short chunks? If token-by-token, do you need partial semantics early (e.g., first 200 tokens) prioritized?
3) Any hard constraints for tail latency during bursts (e.g., no more than 800 ms end-to-end for 99th percentile)?

Next steps I propose:
- Hummingbird shares 10 representative records (sanitized) and a short traffic profile (sample RPS across 24 hours).
- Redwood runs a 2-week SLO qualification POC: (1) baseline latency matrix with your workload on our hosted runtime, (2) streaming vs non-streaming comparisons, (3) fallback model and quantization impacts on quality/econ.
- Schedule 60-min tech deep-dive next Wed (karthik + monica + marissa + your eng lead) to walk the sample traces and define acceptance criteria.

Attachments I can send: a short SLO matrix template and our streaming playbook. I attached the SLO template to this thread; can reformat if helpful.

Thanks — Karthik

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the clear recap. Short answers inline: 

> 1) How often do you hit the 6k bound today vs 3–4k?
We see ~12% of sessions with >5k tokens, about 60% between 2–4k, and the rest <2k. The >5k cases are typically multi-visit histories for complex patients.

> 2) Streaming behavior
We stream at the client per token today; the UI renders in near realtime. We do batch small groups (4–8 tokens) for rendering efficiency but want first-byte latency to be low. Prioritizing the first ~150–200 tokens helps UX a lot.

> 3) Tail latency constraint
Hard constraint: 99th percentile should not exceed 1s for interactive queries; SLA for background tasks can be 2–3s.

We can prepare the 10 sanitized examples tomorrow. Also adding two asks:
- Can Redwood demonstrate progressive decoding that flushes earlier tokens when input >4k?
- We'd like a cost estimate for serving the 12% high-context sessions vs compressed/fallback variants.

I'll loop in our eng lead if the POC plan looks good.

—Alyssa

Hi Alyssa — great to see the numbers, thanks. A few technical notes so expectations are aligned before the deep dive: 

1) Streaming & first-byte prioritization Redwood's runtime supports low-latency streaming and can be tuned to prioritize prefix tokens. For sessions where input > 4k tokens we can enable a progressive flush mode that returns early tokens while the remainder remains in-flight; this reduces perceived latency at the UI.

2) Fallback model options To hit the 99p 1s constraint for interactive queries at scale, we typically recommend a two-path approach: (A) primary model with full 8k context (GPU-optimized quantized float16/INT8) and (B) fallback compressed model with 4k context and smaller KV memory footprint. The fallback can also run on cheaper instances for cost control.

3) Caching & prefix reuse If you have structured chart elements that repeat (e.g., medication lists, problem lists), KV caching yields large savings and reduces the pressure on the context window. We'll want example traces to identify stable prefixes.

4) Load shaping & circuit breakers We'll propose conservative circuit-breaker thresholds for burst windows (e.g., when queue latency >250ms for 10s roll window) that redirect to the fallback model or degrade to non-streamed background generation.

Action items before the deep dive:
- Alyssa: sanitized records + 24h traffic profile (as Karthik requested).
- Redwood: I'll put together a short POC runbook with acceptance criteria and a cost delta estimate for the 12% high-context traffic. Expect a draft by EOD tomorrow.

Attaching: redwood-streaming-playbook.pdf (high-level) and a sample SLO matrix.

—Monica
